items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Professor Mineta was playing sax and I was playing drum... And you say it was in that band that you learned a lot from Professor Mineta? Oh yeah, well he taught me a lot. He taught me a lot.

ctx.x: They had Walter Deku on piano. Emile Biggoin on violin. And they had Bill Matthews was playing drum.

And they had Joe Howard playing trumpet. Was there a clarinet did you mention? Yes. No. No. Who was the clarinet? Who was the clarinet? Was there a clarinet did you mention? The clarinet player was uh, The clarinet player was uh, Louis Nelson. Biggoin. Oh yeah. Oh yeah. Can you tell us anything about your, anything else about your uncle? Uh, when did he die about? I don't even know. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.…

items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] when you ever worked with Professor Mineta... [INTERVIEWEE] He was the leader.

ctx.x: Uh, uh, when Professor Mineta, uh, when you ever worked with Professor Mineta, uh, did you find that, uh, he, he sort of, uh, he was playing piano, did you say in that band? Oh, saxophone. Sax. Uh, did you find that he sort of led the band or, uh, or just played his part or? Oh, he was the leader of the band.
He was the leader. In other words, the old man, the violin was supposed to be the leader but Professor was
the, was the leader. Did, uh, Professor usually, uh, start the band and knock the band off? What's that? Did he usually start the band? Oh yeah, he start the band.
